newsitem.title: USA: NTSB proposes air safety measures after TWA crash.
newsitem.headline: NTSB proposes air safety measures after TWA crash.

text.p: The U.S. National Transportation Safety Board said on Friday TWA Flight 800 was most likely brought down by an explosion of its centre wing fuel tank and recommended safety measures to prevent volatile mixtures of fuel and air.
"The reconstruction thus far shows outward deformation of the internal components of the tank that are consistent with an explosion originating within the tank," the NTSB said.

In a written statement to the Federal Aviation Administration, the NTSB recommended modifications to aircraft design to prevent such fuel tank explosions. The FAA said it would urgently review the board's request.
The Paris-bound TWA Boeing 747 exploded shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy Airport on July 17, killing all 230 people on board.
